summary: You take PSYCH 1 and PSYCH 10, five core courses with at least two from each of Areas A and B, the WIM and a capstone, and electives for 70 units. Electives are PSYCH courses of 3 or more units or the cognates BIO 150, PSYC 135 and PSYC 139; up to 10 units of research, independent study and practica (such as PSYCH 194, 195, 198, 182 and 281) also count, 15 for honors students. At most 10 units may come from outside Psychology, so at least 60 are in the department. Every course needs a letter grade of C- or better unless it is offered only S/NC. Outside courses, a TA's extra research units, and a statistics course standing in for PSYCH 10 because your other program requires it are moved in by hand. Core courses taken in summer, the honors application and thesis, and the no-AP-credit and no-double-counting rules are checked by hand.

program.why: Grading: "All courses towards the 70-unit requirement must be taken for a letter grade of C- or better, except for courses offered only on an S/NC (Satisfactory/No Credit) basis."

totals.label: Units from outside Psychology
totals.why: Policies: "Psychology majors must complete at least 60 units of coursework toward their major at Stanford within the Psychology department. Psychology majors may count no more than a total of ten units of credit from outside the department toward the major". Electives: the three cognate courses "count as PSYCH courses, not outside units". With the 70-unit minimum, a 10-unit cap on outside units is the 60-unit Psychology minimum, cognates included.

cjO4wofK.why: "The remaining unit requirements can be fulfilled through elective PSYCH courses. An elective Psychology course is any PSYCH course that is three units or more (excluding independent study, research, and practicum). There are also three cognate courses from other departments that count as PSYCH courses, not outside units. These courses are: BIO 150, PSYC 135, and PSYC 139". The 70 units ("the 70 units needed for the major") are program.unitsMin, which counts every course the program's rules hold, so this pool takes the rest. Research, independent study and practica (the five the text names, PSYCH 194, 195, 198, 182, 281, and the other PSYCH courses whose catalog titles name them as research projects, independent study or practica) are left out here and counted in ov-research.

A0YPCtGJ.why: "This is a year-long seminar taken in the senior year ... Students may opt for 1-4 units in each of the three quarters." PSYCH 198 is repeatable, so it is listed three times.

fmGYJQGm.why: "Three quarters of Honors Research ... [PSYCH 198] (Senior Honors Research) autumn, winter, and spring quarter". PSYCH 198 is repeatable, so it is listed three times. These are the same three quarters of PSYCH 198 that the Honors capstone option asks for ("students should complete either the Psychology Honors option or Capstone: Psych Applied option"), so the rule shares them.
